basis: Inherited episodic muscle weakness; muscle weakness is obligate, with no evidence establishing another affected axis.
Defined as autoimmune disease affecting the cardiovascular system.
Defining triad of junctional skin blistering, severe interstitial lung disease and nephrotic renal disease.
Ureteral obstruction impairs urinary drainage; ureters and kidneys share the renal axis.
Developmental impairment is common across constitutional 20p/20q deletion syndromes; sparse umbrella data do not establish other shared organ damage.
Skeletal dysplasia defines disease; dental malocclusion/crowding occurs in 12/15 (80%). Cardiac defects are below 30%; microcephaly alone does not prove neurologic injury.
Inflammation of nasal mucosa; the umbrella includes allergic and nonallergic forms, so an immune mechanism is not universal.
Intestinal infection by Moniezia tapeworms; the supplied definition explicitly concerns ruminants.
Transferrin deficiency causes anemia and disordered iron transport. Liver injury frequency is unclear; cardiac/endocrine findings are occasional; infections are separate.
Neurodevelopmental disease; absent thumb 1/1, cardiac defects 1/3 and cleft palate 1/3 support additional axes, but very small denominators limit certainty.
Inherited iron overload commonly causes liver injury and arthropathy (~30-50% in clinical disease); cardiac injury is a minority. Iron deposition alone is insufficient.
Axonal sensorimotor neuropathy; persistent foot deformity occurs in 14/18 (78%), with distal amyotrophy. Scoliosis occurs in only 3/18.
Congenital anterior segment dysgenesis with iris atrophy and pupillary abnormalities; systemic Rieger syndrome features are not implied.
Bone and muscle developmental disorder; intellectual disability and symblepharon each occur in 30-79%. Nevi and pinna shape alone do not establish functional damage.
Diffuse induration of skin and subcutaneous fat; associated neonatal critical illness does not establish direct damage to other organs.
Primary malignant bone tumor, a fibroblastic variant of conventional osteosarcoma.
Embryonal tumor arising in the cerebellopontine angle of the brain.
Species-defined fungal infection; pulmonary and otic localization vary, and the broad definition does not establish a shared damaged organ in at least 30%.
CHMP2B-related frontotemporal neurodegeneration and/or motor neuron disease; behavioral symptoms reflect neurologic disease.
Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with intellectual disability in 5/5 and seizures in 4/5; no common independent organ damage established.
Defining brain, eye and heart defects; oral clefts occur in 80-99%. Cap omits skeletal anomalies (80-99%) and renal/hearing abnormalities (30-79%).
Hereditary disease group defined by neuro-ophthalmic involvement; no evidence supports additional shared organ damage.
Propionate metabolism defect; persistent neurodevelopmental injury affects over 50%. Cardiomyopathy is usually below 30%; crisis-related cytopenias can be transient.
Zellweger spectrum: neurologic injury, hepatic dysfunction and sensorineural hearing loss commonly exceed 30%; retinal disease also qualifies but is omitted by the cap.
Spastic neuropathy and optic atrophy define disease; persistent muscle wasting occurs in 2/2 and Achilles tendon abnormalities in 80-99%.
